She also has a knack for adding to existing stakes when they fall out of favor.

Ark added to its positions in Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI), and Nu Holdings (NYSE: NU). Archer Aviation has surrendered nearly two-thirds of its value over the past year. Archer Aviation's business is literally and figuratively about to take off, but the same can't be said for the stock. Shares of Archer Aviation have been cut nearly in half in 2026. It's a broken IPO, trading 60% below its debut price from five years ago.

The irony is that Archer Aviation stock is ready to break free from its past as a pre-revenue company. Archer Aviation isn't alone. It has partnered with airlines and the U.S. military. It's already struck a deal to be the official air-taxi provider of the 2028 Summer Olympics. Long-term revenue projections have recently been pared back, but it's still an impressive trajectory from here.

Don't ask about earnings at this point. Archer Aviation's cash-rich balance sheet reduces its $3 billion market cap to an enterprise value of only $1.6 billion. The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Tuesday, Oct, 27 2026

US stocks look set for a slightly softer open, with the focus squarely on interest rate expectations rather than overnight equity moves abroad. Sentiment feels cautious as investors weigh solid US activity data against an approaching Fed decision.

The Chicago Fed National Activity Index printed at +0.07 for September, which points to modestly above trend growth. That reading supports the view of a still resilient US economy just one day before the Fed announces its latest interest rate decision.

A firmer growth backdrop can keep borrowing costs elevated, since policymakers have less pressure to cut aggressively when activity indicators run positive. Higher rate expectations tend to bite most in rate sensitive areas such as smaller caps and capital intensive businesses that rely heavily on refinancing.

The unresolved question is simple: Does a +0.07 activity print give the Fed enough confidence to signal a tighter path, or will officials lean on recent volatility in volatility gauges and global data to justify a more cautious tone on future hikes?

MercadoLibre (MELI) shares fell 7.8% on Monday, October 26, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 0.7%. The company released no announcements, earnings reports, or filings. The drop came the day after Brazil's president won a surprise fourth term in Sunday's runoff election, with news reports placing MercadoLibre among the U.S.-listed Brazilian stocks that fell. So why would a vote in Brazil pull down MercadoLibre's shares?

What Ties MercadoLibre To Brazil's Election?

A news report said the U.S.-listed Brazilian companies most exposed to government policy and borrowing costs took the hardest hit from the surprise result. Shares of Brazilian companies fell broadly that Monday, and news reports named MercadoLibre among them.

MercadoLibre maintains operations in Brazil. Management said on the August 5 call that items per buyer on its Brazilian online marketplace grew 19% from a year earlier in Q2 2026. The company is also a lender, and its credit portfolio reached $16.4 billion in Q2, up 75% from a year earlier.

Did Comparable Stocks Fall As Much?

They did not. Four of the five companies on MercadoLibre's peer list fell during the session, but PayPal's 3.6% drop was the largest among them. Amazon was the only one that rose, gaining 0.4%.

The sector moved the other way. XLY, the fund that tracks MercadoLibre's consumer discretionary sector, rose 1.0% that session. MercadoLibre dropped more than twice as much as PayPal, falling far more than its peers while its sector advanced. The stock tracked Brazilian shares instead, though to a lesser degree: a news report said a Brazil ETF fell 20% that Monday.

Where MercadoLibre Stock Stands Now

Declines of this size are uncommon for MercadoLibre. The stock had dropped this much in three other sessions over the prior 365 days, most recently falling 12.7% on May 8, 2026.

Monday's drop deepened a one-year loss. The shares have shed 22.3% over the past year, trailing a 15.3% gain for the S&P 500. They closed at $1,668.72, sitting far below their 52-week closing high of $2,360.76 from October 30, 2025. With a 52-week closing low of $1,546.81 on May 15, 2026, the shares now rest much closer to their low than to their high. Over the three months to October 26, they lost 10.4%, while the S&P 500 gained 3.6%.

Following the decline, MercadoLibre trades at 2.4 times its sales over the past twelve months, coming in below the S&P 500's 3.2 times. MercadoLibre is expected to report its third-quarter 2026 results in November 2026, and the growth of its credit portfolio is the measure to watch.

Investors were anticipating a victory from the business-friendly candidate Flavio Balsonaro in the presidential election in Brazil over the weekend, but that didn't happen.

Instead, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva held on to victory and will remain as president.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Brazilian stocks had one of their worst days on record on Monday in response to the news. The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (NYSE: EWZ) tumbled 19.8% on Monday after trading down more than 25% in morning trading. Some of the fund's biggest holdings include Vale, the global mining company; the fintech company Nu Holdings; and Petrobras, Brazil's oil company.

One of the top stocks out of Brazil is MercadoLibre (Nasdaq: MELI), an e-commerce company that has grown over the years to include a fintech platform, a delivery arm, and a credit business.

MercadoLibre finished Monday down 7.8% after trading down as much as 12.4% earlier in the session. MercadoLibre outperformed Brazilian stocks more broadly, but that makes sense since only about half of the company's business comes from Brazil. Its next two biggest markets are Mexico and Argentina, and the company is expanding across Latin America.

Should investors buy the dip on MercadoLibre? Let's take a closer look.

Image source: MercadoLibre.

Does the sell-off make sense?

It's not unusual for elections to move stock markets, especially when the results are a surprise. However, what is unusual about the fallout from the Brazilian election is that Lula is the incumbent, and his policies would essentially be the status quo.

Bolsonaro had promised fiscal reform, including spending caps, cuts to public spending, and a pledge against new taxes. Whether that would have benefited the Brazilian economy and the stock market, we'll never know.

However, investors who think that Lula's policies have been a problem for MercadoLibre might want to think again. MercadoLibre just became the first company to record 30 straight quarters of 30% or better revenue growth, a testament to its consistency and excellence. It's true that the stock has struggled over the last couple of years, but that is more due to rising competition from the likes of Amazon and Sea Limited's Shopee, and falling profit margins as the company invests in the business.

"I didn't take ​sides, but it looked like another rigged election," U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters following the results. "It looked very bad to me." The President had not officially endorsed any candidates ahead of the elections, but Reuters reported he had led a campaign to bring Bolsonaro back to power.

Uber Technologies: Demonstrating a Steady Quarterly Revenue Uptrend

Uber Technologies generates revenue by connecting users with independent ride-hailing drivers and local delivery services.

It announced a definitive agreement to acquire the corporate catering marketplace ezCater for $2.3 billion in cash, and initiated a workforce restructuring plan affecting approximately 3,300 roles globally.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Foolish Take

Investors should take notice of the revenue trend favoring MercadoLibre. I happen to own stock in both MercadoLibre and Uber, and I see potential and uncertainty for both consumer discretionary stocks.

MercadoLibre operates in the turbulent Latin America region, which has historically brought with it political and economic risks. The stock took a hit on Monday, Oct. 26, following the reelection of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on the previous day. Brazil accounted for over half of MercadoLibre's revenue in the second quarter of 2026.
